news.title: South Korea’s football association apologises, vows ‘sweeping reform’ after World Cup debacle
news.lede: The association has been engulfed in a widening crisis since South Korea’s disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign. SEOUL – The Korea Football Association (KFA) formally apologised to football fans and officials and pledged sweeping reforms on Aug 8 as controversies over its governance and alleged misconduct continued to mount. The fallout has included the first National Assembly hearing on the KFA, a police raid and newly surfaced allegations involving sexual entertainment for foreign referees and match officials more than a decade ago. The KFA’s governance and management came under scrutiny at the National Assembly hearing on July 30, which examined, among other issues, the contentious appointments of former national team coaches Hong Myung-bo and Jurgen Klinsmann.

news.title: 'Will Blow Up Messi With Four Bombs': Dossier Reveals Chilling FIFA World Cup Plot Targeting Argentine Star
news.lede: Argentine captain Lionel Messi was among the footballers singled out in a series of serious security threats during the recent FIFA World Cup 2026 that was co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and USA. Citing a police dossier detailing incidents that they monitored during the tournament, a report claimed there were threats against players, officials and their families, with Messi reportedly facing some of the most specific threats recorded. One threat involved a caller who allegedly told authorities that he and two other people were travelling to the stadium in Dallas carrying homemade bombs and an AR-15 rifle. The caller reportedly said the intended targets included police officers and players from both teams, while specifically naming Messi.

news.title: From bomb threats against Messi to a Ronaldo hotel breach, a secret dossier reveals how close the World Cup came to being a catastrophe
news.lede: From bomb threats targeting Lionel Messi to a stalker breaching Cristiano Ronaldo’s hotel, a leaked police dossier has exposed just how close the 2026 FIFA World Cup came to disaster. According to The Sun, the chilling document, obtained by Informacion.es, reveals a wave of terror plots, death threats, and security breaches that turned the tournament into a high-stakes game of cat-and-mouse with extremists, overzealous fans, and even disgruntled referees. The most alarming threats centered on Argentina’s national team, with Messi bearing the brunt. Before Argentina’s match against Jordan, a man called Dallas airport and declared he and two accomplices would storm the stadium armed with “homemade bombs and an AR-15.”

news.title: Norway Football Federation Calls on FIFA Chief to Resign Over Failed World Cup Plan
news.lede: ISTANBUL, Aug 8 – Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness called on Friday for FIFA President Gianni Infantino to resign, saying he had lost the federation’s confidence, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing media reports. “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” Klaveness told The Guardian following the NFF’s monthly board meeting. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino,” she said.

news.title: Lionel Messi alone will decide when to retire: Argentine football president
news.lede: Messi would turn 43 years old during the 2030 World Cup. Especially after witnessing what Lionel Messi was still capable of at this summer’s World Cup, the president of the Argentina Football Association is not rushing the all-time great out the door. Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia said in an interview on Argentine TV uploaded on Aug 7 that Messi is the only person making the decision when to hang up his boots. “It’s a decision that is purely and personally his,” Tapia said, according to a translation.

news.title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots
news.lede: It has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010. There are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino was taking his victory lap on Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.

news.title: Norwegian Football Federation president calls for Infantino to resign
news.lede: Norway FA president Lise Klaveness has called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign, saying there is no trust in his leadership, even after he walked back his plan to sell shares of the World Cup to private investors. Infantino unveiled the scheme, branded FIFA Forward Enterprise, shortly after a financially successful Men's World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada. But the idea generated a backlash, with UEFA threatening to boycott FIFA competitions - a threat still on the table even after Infantino withdrew the proposal and said Wednesday, August 5 that he apologized. But Klaveness said the apology didn't feel sincere, and the Norwegian Football Federation board is calling for the president to step down.

news.title: Infantile Infantino should exit for trying to sell the World Cup, By Owei Lakemfa
news.lede: The UEFA knockout punch was its decision to boycott FIFA if the Infantino team went ahead with its greedy plans.
